author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. dollar rose against major currencies Monday as Middle East conflict lifted oil prices and investors prepared for what could be the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate increase in more than two years, Reuters reported.
The dollar index was up 0.3% at 99.41 in the report after touching 99.735, its highest level since Sept. 2. Those figures describe Reuters’ Monday market report and are not a live quote.

Brent crude rose as much as 5% to $109.80 a barrel before giving back part of the gain and trading at $105.61. The move pushed global bond yields higher and reinforced concern that energy costs could keep inflation elevated.

Money markets were pricing about a 90% chance of a Fed rate hike on Wednesday, up from roughly 60% a week earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool cited by Reuters. The shift supported the dollar but also increased uncertainty for stocks and bonds.

The yen weakened 0.5% against the dollar to 154.355 after recent gains, while bitcoin rose 2% to $79,152.23 in the same report. Markets remain sensitive to developments in the conflict, oil flows and the Fed’s decision.
dek: The U.S. dollar index was up 0.3% at 99.41 in Reuters’ Monday report as investors weighed Middle East oil risks and a possible Fed hike.
headline: Dollar gains as oil, rate-hike expectations reshape market mood
